Gaussian mixture clustering of shapes with a variance per cluster

Source: R/shape_mixture.R
shape_mixture.Rd

Clusters \(k \times m \times n\) landmark configurations with a Gaussian mixture with spherical covariance \(\sigma_h^2 I\) for each cluster (model "VII" of mclust) in the leading principal components of the tangent coordinates. The EM algorithm is implemented here, with safeguards for duplicated rows, tiny groups and degenerate components.

Usage

shape_mixture(
  X,
  K,
  var_explained = 0.9,
  max_dim = 10L,
  model = "VII",
  nstart = 10L,
  init = c("kmeans++", "kmeans", "random"),
  iter.max = 200L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  var_floor = 1e-06,
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

X

Numeric array of dimension \(k \times m \times n\), with \(m\) equal to 2 or 3.

K

Number of clusters (>= 2).

var_explained

Proportion of tangent variance that fixes the number of principal components (default 0.90).

max_dim

Largest number of components kept (default 10). The number used is at least max(2, K - 1), as in shape_ensemble.

model

Covariance model. Only "VII" (spherical, unequal volume) is implemented.

nstart

Number of EM starts (default 10); the best log-likelihood among starts without a variance at the floor is kept.

init

Initialization of each start: "kmeans++" (default, k-means++ seeding, nearest-seed labels), "kmeans" (seeding followed by Lloyd iterations) or "random" (random labels).

iter.max

Maximum EM iterations per start (default 200).

tol

Relative log-likelihood tolerance for convergence (default 1e-8).

var_floor

Variance floor, as a fraction of the mean per-dimension variance of the scores (default 1e-6).

seed

Optional integer seed. The caller's random-number stream is restored on exit. With NULL the current stream is used.

...

Not used; reserved.

Value

An object of class "shape_mixture", a list with

cluster

Integer vector of length n, maximum posterior label.

posterior

n x K matrix of posterior probabilities.

means

K x dim matrix of component means in score coordinates.

variances

Length-K vector of spherical variances.

proportions

Length-K vector of mixing proportions.

loglik

Log-likelihood of the fit.

dim

Number of principal components used.

representative

Integer vector of length K: index of the real observation closest (Riemannian \(\rho\)) to the Procrustes mean of each cluster.

centers

Array \(k \times m \times K\) with the cluster means.

converged

Whether EM met the tolerance.

fallback

TRUE if the k-means fallback was used.

K, model, var_explained

The options used.

Details

The scores are those of shape_ensemble: tangent coordinates at the Procrustes mean, then PCA, with the smallest number of components reaching var_explained, between max(2, K - 1) and max_dim.

Why a variance per cluster: k-means (and so a k-means ensemble) assigns to the nearest center, which is the Bayes rule only when all clusters have the same spread. With unequal spread the Bayes boundary is a sphere around the compact cluster and the bisector misassigns the tail of the diffuse one. This model estimates that spread.

Safeguards. Variances are floored at var_floor times the mean per-dimension variance of the scores, so duplicated rows (bootstrap resamples) or a group of identical points never make the likelihood singular. A component with less than one observation of total weight is restarted at the observation worst explained by the current model (at most 5 * K restarts per start, then that start is abandoned). Starts that end with a variance at the floor are treated as likelihood spikes and are used only if no regular start exists. If no start succeeds, the partition is the k-means (5 starts) partition with per-group spherical variances, fallback is TRUE and converged is FALSE.

See also

shape_ensemble, shape_kmeans

Examples

sim <- sim_shapes3d(n = 40, sigma = 1, k = 8, seed = 1)
fit <- shape_mixture(sim$X, K = 2, seed = 1)
fit$variances
#> [1] 0.001442267 0.002163340
table(sim$group, fit$cluster)
#>    
#>      1  2
#>   1  0 40
#>   2 40  0
